failure_summary.description: A verbatim archive answer was in the context but not copied exactly. One run took a forum reply ('Friction') over the archived 'A: the atmosphere'. The other shortened 'a eucalyptus tree' to 'Eucalyptus' under the Rule 4 shortening rules.

Slot-type gaps. A lone quoted catchphrase ('Yabba Dabba Do!') got a passage title containing it instead of the show. A clue describing what 'he' did got the title of the thing he wrote instead of the person. Single-quote clues are only covered for lists.
The clue said a title was altered ('changed All to Oil'). The agent answered with the altered title from the passages instead of the original.

The agent went with the volume of noisy passages in another sense. 'Cyclone State' was read as Iowa because of Iowa State sports pages, although reference lists put it under Kansas. A bare definition ('An Anglican parish priest') got a subordinate role (Curate) instead of the term the glossary passages tie to that exact role.
Gold key is a surname only ('Fragonard') while the agent gave the full name. Formatting variance; not worth a rule.

patch.reasoning: Two failures involve a verbatim archive answer that the agent ignored or shortened. The Rule 3 vs Rule 4 conflict and the forum-vs-archive priority need an explicit fix. Three more failures are slot-type errors where a passage title or work was given instead of the owner, the person, or the original. The last two failures involve choosing by passage volume instead of by the most authoritative or definitional passage. Earlier attempts at a mandatory template were rejected, so these edits are targeted rules placed inside existing Rules 2, 3 and 4. Each is keyed to a visible clue feature, so stable passes should not regress.

edits.target: ## Rule 3: Look for the clue repeated verbatim in the context
edits.content: - PRIORITY ORDER: (1) archive/flashcard/dump lines that reproduce the clue and give an answer ('| a eucalyptus tree.', 'A: the atmosphere', 'CLUE, THE ATMOSPHERE'), (2) reference passages, (3) forum comments, quizzes' user replies ('Friction. Reply. Report Abuse'), contestant replies ('What is gravity?'), (4) your own guess. Never let a lower level beat a higher one. COPY the archived answer character for character, keeping a leading 'a/an/the' and a trailing generic noun ('a eucalyptus tree', not 'Eucalyptus'; 'the atmosphere', not 'Friction' or 'atmosphere'). Quote the matched line before the answer tags.

edits.target: ## Rule 4: Exact-match formatting of the final answer
edits.content: - EXEMPTION: every shortening or delete-clue-words rule below applies ONLY when no verbatim archive answer exists (Rule 3). If an archive line gives the answer, do not shorten, drop articles, or drop the generic noun.

edits.target: ## Rule 2: Answer the referent, not a word from the clue
edits.content:
- A clue that is ONLY a quoted catchphrase or exclamation ('"Yabba Dabba Do!"') asks for the show, film or character that owns it. Never answer with a passage title that merely contains the quote (an episode, song or video).
- A clue about what 'he/she' did ('he wrote an explanation of why he would kill X', 'she painted...') asks for the PERSON. The work he or she made (a poem, letter, painting) is an anchor, never the answer.
- A clue that says a title or phrase was 'changed', 'altered', 'parodied' or 'swapped' ('changed "All" to "Oil" in this title') asks for the ORIGINAL, unaltered title or phrase ('All's Well That Ends Well'). Do not answer with the altered version that the passages show.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - Nickname or definition clues: weight passages by kind, not by count. A passage that lists the term under its owner (a nickname list 'Kansas: Cyclone State', a glossary 'vicar: the priest in charge of a parish') beats many passages that use the same word in another sense (sports teams, schools, products, fan pages). For a bare definition ('An Anglican parish priest'), answer the term the glossaries tie to that exact role, not a related subordinate or different role (an assistant, a deputy, a visitor).
